verdict.rationale: Proa's own docs show first-party client state through signals in hydrated islands, which ship with seed state and a shared runtime. WebContext also gives typed access to route state. These are built-in framework primitives, not a documented state management library maintained alongside the framework, so only the core idea is evidenced. Missing for 10: a named official state management library or package, documentation of shared or global store patterns, cross-island state sharing, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use an official first-party state management library maintained alongside the framework

citations.quote: Add signals and event handlers, and Proa emits the server-rendered HTML plus the JavaScript required for that island
Each hydrated RSJS island emits a small vanilla-JS module plus seed state, served with a shared runtime around 1.3 KB gzipped.
Every render has typed access to request-scoped data, response metadata, route state, and loader caching through the same WebContext
